title: At Ramayana's Mumbai Screening, Lakshman Ravi Dubey Seeks Hanuman Sunny Deol's Blessings
excerpt: Dubey touched Deol's feet at the star-studded special screening on November 3 — a moment fans instantly framed as Lakshman honouring Hanuman, two days before the film's worldwide release.
body:
• At a special Mumbai screening of Ramayana: Part 1 on Tuesday, November 3, Ravi Dubey — the film's Lakshman — touched the feet of Sunny Deol, who plays Hanuman, and sought his blessings.
  • Fans online framed the moment in the film's own terms: Lakshman seeking the blessings of Hanuman.
  • The screening drew Ranbir Kapoor (Rama), Alia Bhatt, Neetu Kapoor, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and director Nitesh Tiwari.
  • The Hindi film opens worldwide on Thursday, November 5, with paid previews on November 4.

It was the photograph of the night. At the special screening of Ramayana: Part 1 in Mumbai on Tuesday, November 3, actor Ravi Dubey arrived with his wife Sargun Mehta and, on meeting Sunny Deol, bent to touch his feet and seek his blessings — a gesture of respect to a senior that photographers captured and fans immediately read through the film itself. Dubey plays Lakshman in Nitesh Tiwari's epic; Deol plays Hanuman. As the Times of India's headline put it, it looked like "Laxman seeking blessings from Hanuman," and the images travelled fast online.

The screening

The Mumbai screening, held two days before release, brought together the film's cast and families: Ranbir Kapoor, who plays Rama, arrived with Alia Bhatt and Neetu Kapoor; Sai Pallavi plays Sita and Yash plays Ravana in the film. Also in attendance were Kajal Aggarwal with her son, Rakul Preet Singh with Jackky Bhagnani, Lara Dutta, Kunal Kapoor, Vivek Oberoi and director Nitesh Tiwari, according to Pinkvilla and India Forums. The Mumbai event followed earlier premieres in Los Angeles on October 27 and in London.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ArZO7yY2Jf4

The film

Ramayana: Part One is a Hindi-language adaptation of the epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. It is the first of two parts, with the concluding chapter slated for Diwali 2027. The film opens in theatres worldwide on Thursday, November 5, with paid previews on November 4 — which makes Tuesday's screening the industry's first full look at a production carrying a reported ₹4,000 crore of investment and expectation. Whatever the reviews say on Thursday, the Dubey–Deol moment has already given the release its defining image of respect between generations: the younger actor honouring the senior, in character and out of it.
